articles.title: Universiteit Gent is in 2029 gastheer van grootste archeologiecongres ter wereld
articles.snippet: De UGent organiseert in september 2029 het congres van de grootste internationale beroepsvereniging voor archeologen. Gent en Vlaanderen worden dan enkele dagen het internationale centrum van de archeologische wereld. Het congres brengt naar verwachting 3.000 tot 4.000 archeologen, erfgoedspecialisten en beleidsmakers uit de hele wereld naar Gent. Het is de eerste keer dat het evenement in België plaatsvindt.
articles.summary: De UGent organiseert in september 2029 het congres van de grootste internationale beroepsvereniging voor archeologen. Gent en Vlaanderen worden dan enkele dagen het internationale centrum van de archeologische wereld.

articles.title: Women in UK arts feel they do not have equal opportunities for roles, says report
articles.snippet: Exclusive: Research says sector is fixated with young talent, with most women experiencing unconscious bias or sexism Women working in the arts believe they do not have equal opportunities for roles, especially as they get older, according to a report saying that the industry is fixated with “young and emerging” talent. Nearly all (95%) women working in the arts thought gender inequality persisted, while three-quarters (75%) reported experiencing unconscious bias or sexism, according to a survey of 76 arts professionals. More than two-thirds (69%) felt that age negatively affected their career success – a figure that rose to 100% among those working in artistic rather than managerial roles.

articles.title: How to make a bestseller: insiders reveal the tricks of the book trade
articles.snippet: From cover design to shelf placement and influencer partnerships … how publishers will persuade you to buy their books this autumn Think about the last book you bought. How did you choose it? Was it from a recommendation, a review, a TikTok video? Did the cover grab you, were you swayed by the quotes on the front, or did you just happen to spot it on an appealing table as you walked into the shop? Did you think about all the nudges that led you to that decision – by the publisher, the bookseller or that person you follow on Insta? articles.title: Households could save up to £173 a year by switching to fixed energy deal
articles.snippet: Moving tariffs will cushion the blow from the October price cap rise and the increase widely predicted for January With higher energy bills looming and warnings of worse to come in the new year, many households could save up to £173 a year by switching to a fixed deal. Millions of households in Great Britain will face the highest energy charges in three years after it was announced that the government’s price cap will rise again in October. This will be the second increase in three months. Continue reading...

articles.title: ‘Winter panic’: EU gas stores at their lowest level in 13 years
articles.snippet: As one of Europe’s biggest consumers of gas the UK may be particularly exposed to heightened price volatility Europe is on course to enter the cooler months with gas stores at their lowest level in 13 years, which has triggered “winter panic” among energy traders, experts have warned. The EU’s gas stocks were 63% full in the last week of August, well below the 80% average for late August over recent years and among the lowest levels ever recorded for this time of year.
